a9b49f416230: Ready-to-import JSON configurations for MultiDatePick, the most customizable calendar component suite for Salesforce. Covers date selection, time scheduling, and resource booking use cases across HR, education, healthcare, real estate, operations, and more.
54f0ed1aa223: <t1>41 ready-to-import configs</t1> for every common scheduling scenario, each with its views already chosen. Copy one into the Setup Wizard, then use it by its Config Name on a Lightning page, an Experience site or a Flow screen. Field names map to your org in a click.

c9974a978518: Volunteers mark the dates they're available. Date range consolidation means a week of availability becomes one record instead of five. Recurring patterns let volunteers say "every Saturday" through the end of the quarter.
0d50b515183e: Compliance teams schedule audit dates for accounts. Multi-day audits use date range consolidation. Hover tooltips show the assigned auditor and audit type at a glance. Status colors track progress from planned through completion or failure.
9b0d88c1b3ce: Managers assign on-call coverage across a team. Recurring patterns make it easy to set weekly rotations. Status colors distinguish primary, secondary, and backup roles at a glance on the calendar.
b0d73b196530: Attendees pick the days they'll attend a multi-day conference. Adjacent days collapse into a single pass record with a start date and end date. A 3-day attendee gets one pass record. Non-adjacent picks (e.g. only Day 1 + Day 3) each get their own record.

4f0936ba3723: Operations managers build shift schedules across a team. Extended hours (6 AM to 10 PM) cover all shift types. Recurring patterns enable weekly rotation templates. Different times per date let managers mix morning and evening shifts.
fbb6b2d92c60: Service businesses schedule client appointments with conflict prevention. Status colors show confirmed, pending, and cancelled slots at a glance. Hover tooltips reveal appointment type and notes without clicking.

08cb7374e203: <t1>Time Grid Only mode:</t1> <t2>Time Grid Only</t2> hides the calendar and shows just the time-slot grid for one implied date. The date comes from <t3>Time Grid Date Field</t3> (here <t4>Event_Date__c</t4> on the host record); set an explicit <t5>Time Grid Date</t5> instead, or omit both to fall back to today. Best on a record page where the date is already known.
79c860b098dd: IT teams schedule overnight maintenance windows for assets and infrastructure. Conflict behavior is set to "allow" instead of "block", so teams can intentionally overlap maintenance if needed. Hover fields show change number, description, and impact assessment.
ca81db1a2e5d: <t1>Overnight time range:</t1> <t2>Earliest Time</t2> 22:00 → <t3>Latest Time</t3> 06:00 crosses midnight. Slot generation handles this; verify the calendar renders the way you expect before training admins.
f82a2a98f967: <t1>End Date Field API Name</t1> multi-day windows <t2>endDateField</t2>
ead457b0d1fc: Real estate agents schedule property showings. Different times per date let agents block different windows for different properties. Hover tooltips show the assigned agent and buyer name without opening the record.
46894fba316b: Professors or advisors publish their office hours on a calendar. 15-minute slots provide granular scheduling. Recurring patterns let instructors set "Mon/Wed/Fri 2-4 PM" for the entire semester in one click.
7cdaa3badf07: Academic departments schedule exam sessions for courses. Conflict detection prevents scheduling two exams in the same slot. Status colors track progress from scheduled through completion. Hover shows assigned room and proctor.
6d74dd9e0dbc: For shifts with mandated rest periods (DOT, healthcare, manufacturing). The shift saves as one parent record covering the full envelope; required rest periods become child sub-block records that auditors can review. 15-minute granularity for fine-grained rest tracking.
0bca700452e1: <t1>Sub-Blocks:</t1> rest periods are stored as child records on the bundled <t2>Sub_Block__c</t2> object. No extra schema setup required. Point <t3>Sub-Block Object API Name</t3> at your own child object if you'd rather use a custom name.
e5a36f2e04fe: End-user appointment picker that automatically grays out dates the office is closed. Reads its block list from <t1>Office Closure Calendar</t1> records via <t2>Blocked Dates Object</t2>, <t3>Blocked Dates Filter Field</t3> and <t4>Blocked Dates Filter Value</t4>, so customers can only book on days that are actually open.
d433c67b29f4: <t1>Pairs with <t2>Office Closure Calendar</t2>:</t1> the manager-facing closures config writes <t3>Status__c = Cancelled</t3> records into <t4>Schedule__c</t4>. This config reads them with <t5>Blocked Dates Filter Field</t5> set to <t6>Status__c</t6> and <t7>Blocked Dates Filter Value</t7> set to <t8>Cancelled</t8>, and hides them from its own view with <t9>Ignored Statuses</t9> set to <t10>Cancelled</t10> so users only see real appointments.
68763a5887bd: No Date Time configs match this filter.
857d7f741664: Configs for Booking: date and time selection with resource management. Best for rooms, equipment, people, facilities, and anything with availability or capacity limits.
90689f0721fb: Employees reserve conference rooms with live capacity badges. Status colors distinguish confirmed, pending, and cancelled bookings. Cancelled bookings are hidden from the grid and don't count toward capacity.
dfa0fd5ddc70: Resource booking where closures can be <t1>partial-day</t1> (block specific hours, not the whole day) and <t2>per-resource</t2> (close just one resource, leaving the rest bookable). Reads closures from a dedicated <t3>Office Closure</t3> object, scoped per location via the resource + region filters.
a8292081e2d4: <t1>Closure object:</t1> create <t2>Office_Closure__c</t2> records with a <t3>Closure_Date__c</t3>, optional <t4>Closure_Start_Time__c</t4> + <t5>Closure_End_Time__c</t5> (omit both for a whole-day close), a <t6>Region__c</t6> tag, and an optional <t7>Resource__c</t7> lookup (set = that resource only; blank = all resources in the region).
117fc32570f3: IT or AV teams manage shared equipment reservations. 60-minute slots cover typical checkout durations. Business hours fields ensure equipment is only bookable during operating hours.
c865feb8aa58: <t1>Business Hours Start Field</t1> / <t2>Business Hours End Field</t2> <t3>businessHoursStartField, businessHoursEndField</t3>
9124806be07a: Employees reserve shared desks in a hybrid workplace. The time slot grid is disabled, so desks are booked for the full day. Capacity tracking shows how many seats remain at shared tables. Two-month view helps plan weeks ahead.
34812bf89c40: <t1>Date-only Booking:</t1> <t2>Disable Time Slot Grid (Full-Day Mode)</t2> removes the hourly slot grid entirely. Best when bookings are full-day and capacity is the only constraint. Combine with <t3>Capacity Field</t3> to model any shared inventory (desks, lockers, parking spots).
6f3251dbc526: Research labs, recording studios, or maker spaces with capacity limits. Status colors distinguish between reserved, in-use, and maintenance slots. Hover tooltips show the purpose and equipment needed for each booking.
1e9f0c8fc398: Fleet managers handle vehicle checkout for field teams. Extended hours (6 AM to 8 PM) accommodate early departures and late returns. Consolidated time span merges adjacent slots into a single booking block. Hover shows purpose and destination.
35087b65e4f6: Healthcare practices schedule therapy sessions per therapist. Recurring patterns let patients book a standing weekly session. Cancelled bookings are hidden from the grid. Availability badges show each therapist's open slots.
2026b865a3b5: Gyms, courts, and fields with capacity limits. Extended hours (6 AM to 10 PM) cover early-morning and evening sessions. Multiple resources enabled so members can book a court and a batting cage in one flow.
52873a3731fa: <t1>Multi-resource mode:</t1> <t2>Allow Booking Multiple Resources</t2> swaps the single-resource dropdown for checkboxes. The time grid renders combined capacity across whatever resources the user has selected, and bookings can span multiple resources atomically.
91f9b6c052d5: A trainer leads ONE session that runs simultaneously across linked rooms (overflow seating, hybrid sites, livestream studios). With <t1>Capacity Aggregation</t1> set to <t2>Distinct</t2>, picking 4 rooms for a 2 PM session shows <t3>1/MAX-cap</t3>: one event across four rooms, so the count tracks distinct sessions rather than per-room inventory.
35b1d99b54ca: <t1>When to pick Distinct vs Combined:</t1> use <t2>Distinct</t2> when one logical event uses several resources together (a workshop running in 4 rooms = 1 booking). Use the default <t3>Combined</t3> when resources contribute independently (a catering bundle with 3 ovens + 2 warmers sums to 5 used).
b9830194c5e8: Showcases <t1>Resource Filter Field</t1> + <t2>Resource Filter Value</t2> with the <t3>multi-field AND</t3> syntax. The picker shows only resources where <t4>Active__c = true</t4> AND <t5>Resource_Type__c = 'Conference Room'</t5>. The semicolon separator combines both filters; admins can swap in any field/value pair from the resource object.
2adbee911a8d: <t1>Filter syntax cheatsheet:</t1> <t2>;</t2> between fields = AND, <t3>,</t3> between values = OR. Field count on each side of <t4>;</t4> must match. Examples: <t5>Resource_Type__c=Conference Room</t5> · <t6>Building__c=North,South</t6> (OR) · <t7>Resource_Type__c;Building__c=Conference Room;North,South</t7> (AND with OR inside the second field).
f119587fa10a: Reserve multiple independent pieces of equipment (ovens, warmers, serving stations, beverage carts) for the same event. Each item has its own capacity, and <t1>Capacity Aggregation</t1> set to <t2>Combined</t2> sums everything, so 3 ovens used out of 5 oven inventory + 2 warmers used out of 4 reads as <t3>5/9</t3> across the bundle.
4b2ec2f453b3: <t1>Multi-resource + Combined capacity (default):</t1> sums bookings AND capacities across the checked resources. The "5/9" badge tells operators they have 4 spots left across the whole bundle without having to mentally add up per-resource counts.
76ea4b9c7dcb: Clients book appointments with specific stylists or therapists. Auto-jump takes users straight to the first available slot. Both cancelled and no-show bookings are hidden from the grid. Hover shows service type, estimated duration, and notes.
aeaab242df45: Customers reserve a vehicle for multiple consecutive days. Adjacent days collapse into a single reservation record per vehicle. A Mon to Fri rental creates one record (start: Mon, end: Fri) instead of five separate daily records. No time slots since the rental spans full days.
8b15aa4c5440: <t1>Date-span Booking without a time grid:</t1> <t2>End Date Field</t2> + <t3>Disable Time Slot Grid (Full-Day Mode)</t3> together model a multi-day rental as a single record with start/end. One Mon to Fri rental is one row, which keeps reports simple.
752785033250: <t1>End Date Field</t1> one record per range <t2>endDateField</t2>
f9580adf0669: <t1>Disable Time Slot Grid (Full-Day Mode)</t1> full-day mode <t2>disableTimeSlotGrid</t2>
88bc4007ec93: Trainers book a full day on a resource (room, vehicle, equipment). The day saves as one parent record from the first slot to the last; lunch and breaks become child sub-block records. Click "Mark as Break" to flag a slot manually, or just leave gaps and they auto-detect.
478cc8c81219: <t1>Sub-Blocks on Booking:</t1> the bundled <t2>Sub_Block__c</t2> child object stores break records linked to the parent Schedule via <t3>Sub-Block Parent Lookup Field</t3>. No extra schema setup required: both objects ship in the package.
93a5b2569d93: Field technicians schedule visits where on-site time and travel-between-stops both matter. The visit envelope saves as one parent record; gaps between picked slots become child sub-block records labeled as travel. Track on-site time vs. drive time separately on the same booking.
73246d03ba47: <t1>Heaviest config in the library:</t1> full Sub-Block support on Booking. Schedule, resource, and sub-block objects all bundled with the package. Reporting can roll up on-site time vs. drive time without custom joins.
b187ea191d74: Dispatchers batch-assign technicians and vehicles across 20+ job sites in one pass. Some sites are already at capacity. With <t1>Conflict Behavior</t1> set to <t2>skip</t2>, the save quietly books the open sites and skips the full ones instead of failing the whole batch. <t3>Allow Booking Multiple Resources</t3> shows the site list as checkboxes with combined capacity counts.
571011dc82c6: <t1>Why skip for bulk dispatch:</t1> across dozens of sites, hitting <t2>block</t2> would reject the entire assignment the moment ONE site is full. <t3>Skip</t3> saves what it can: open sites get booked and full sites are reported back as skipped, so a dispatcher never re-runs the whole batch over a single conflict.
1aa209b4203b: Enroll a learner across a multi-week course where each session has a seat cap and some are already full. With <t1>Conflict Behavior</t1> set to <t2>skip</t2>, batch-selecting sessions enrolls in every open one and skips the at-capacity sessions in one save. <t3>Two-Month View</t3> spans the schedule and combined capacity counts show seats left per session.
abffd35e74f0: <t1>Skip vs block for capacity-limited enrollment:</t1> <t2>skip</t2> lets a learner grab every open session in one click while full sessions are silently passed over. <t3>block</t3> would force them to deselect each full session by hand before the save would go through.
f1acd83dbeaa: Point the resource lookup at <t1>User</t1> and the component becomes people scheduling rather than room booking. Opens on the Utilization heatmap so a manager sees who is over capacity before assigning anything, then switches to Timeline for the month per person or Week to place work at a specific hour.
5cc4371e1621: <t1>User as the resource:</t1> <t2>Resource Object API Name</t2> is <t3>User</t3> with <t4>Resource Filter Field</t4> <t5>IsActive</t5> set to <t6>true</t6>. Capacity has no standard equivalent on User, so add a custom <t7>Daily_Capacity__c</t7> field or the heatmap shows counts instead of percentages. <t8>Business Hours Start Field</t8> and <t9>Business Hours End Field</t9> on User drive per-person working hours in the Week grid.
577bd8c31e32: Two weeks of dates across the top, staff down the side. Opens on Timeline because the question a shift manager asks is who is working when, not what is happening on the 14th. Week places a shift at an exact hour with conflict blocking on; Agenda gives a chronological read for a shift handover.
18065e302260: A wall display or an exec summary. Every offered view is read only or read first, edit mode is off so nobody books from it by accident, and past dates are allowed so the board can look backwards as well as forwards.
3b0adbda1bc2: <t1>Read-only by construction:</t1> Utilization and Agenda cannot write at all, and <t2>Enable Edit Mode</t2> is <t3>false</t3>. Timeline stays available because a 30 day window of every resource is the most useful single screen on a wall, but nothing here saves a record.
5d0a9551887f: The person <t1>is</t1> the resource. Every advisor, rep, consultant or account manager becomes a bookable row, so a client meeting is scheduled against a real Salesforce user rather than a room. Opens on Week because a 30 minute appointment is a time-of-day question; Timeline answers who has room this week, and Agenda is the chronological read for a morning huddle.
905b316d2db2: <t1>User as the resource:</t1> <t2>Resource Object API Name</t2> is <t3>User</t3>, filtered by a custom <t4>Is_Advisor__c</t4> checkbox so the picker holds advisors rather than every active user in the org. <t5>Business Hours Start Field</t5> and <t6>Business Hours End Field</t6> on User give each person their own working day, so the Week grid draws the hours they actually work. <t7>Conflict Behavior</t7> is <t8>block</t8>, because a person can never be double booked.
